title: Grid-search + automated regression detector for batching & KV-cache configs
creator: Marco Reyes
description:
Purpose: build a reproducible grid-search evaluation harness and an automated regression detector that flags quality regressions caused by batching and KV-cache configuration changes. Unlike prior one-off sweeps, this work creates a repeatable pipeline that runs nightly on both synthetic trace workloads and a stratified sample of production requests. Goals: (1) map latency/cost/quality Pareto frontiers across config space; (2) detect regressions vs baseline when a config or model change is proposed; (3) provide triage artifacts (example traces, diffed outputs, failure clusters) to accelerate remediation.

Scope: microbatch_size (1..16), batch_timeout_ms (0..200), prefix_cache_ttl_s (0..7200), kv_cache_eviction_policy (LRU/LFU), prefix_sharding (1..8). We intentionally include non-power-of-two sharding and aggressive TTLs to find edge cases. The harness will evaluate both streaming and non-streaming generation paths and include token-by-token latency profiles for KV-cache hits/misses.

Why this is different: existing sweep tickets focused on single axes (batching or cache TTL). This ticket unifies axes, adds a machine-classifier-based regression detector (trained on historical diffs) to reduce noisy alerts, and produces human-actionable evidence bundles for each detected regression.

Deliverables: reproducible grid-search job definition (k8s CronJob + notebook), nightly CI job that runs the detector and posts results to a dashboard, alerting integration (Slack + issue creation) when regression score exceeds threshold, and a small triage CLI that developers can run locally to reproduce a flagged configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Grid search runs end-to-end on a 1000-sample production-stratified trace and produces a CSV with latency p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token estimate, and quality metrics for each config point
Automated detector runs on nightly outputs and raises < 5 false positives/week on held-out historical changes
Dashboard shows Pareto frontier with links to top 10 worst-regressed traces and example diffs
When threshold exceeded, system creates a Linear ticket with attached evidence bundle and tags runtime-owners
Local triage CLI reproduces exact failure for a given config in under 10 minutes on dev GPU
success_metrics: Detector precision >= 0.8 on historical regression set
Time-to-triage for detected regressions reduced from avg 3d to < 8h
Nightly job completes within 2h for 1000-sample trace
Reduction in config-induced production incidents by 30% over next quarter
eval_plan: 1) Build dataset: sample 1k requests stratified by seq_len, model_type, customer_tier; include 200 golden eval prompts for quality-sensitive features (summarization, instruction-following).

2) Define grid: permutations of microbatch_size, batch_timeout_ms, prefix_cache_ttl_s, kv_cache_eviction_policy, prefix_sharding. Target ~600 config points for nightly run (heuristic pruning applied).
3) Run baseline: capture baseline metrics for current default config across the dataset (latency p50/p95/p99, cost, generation quality via semantic similarity and task-specific metrics).

4) For each config point: execute generation, collect per-request latency traces, token-level KV cache hit/miss stats, output text, and deterministic seeds. Compute quality metrics: semantic similarity (embedding cosine vs gold), edit distance for short-answer tasks, and task-specific accuracy for closed tasks.
5) Aggregation: compute delta vs baseline for latency and quality. Produce multi-objective score (user-configurable weightings) and compute Pareto frontier.

6) Regression detector: featurize diffs (average quality delta, worst-case example delta, variance across customer segments) and run classifier that outputs regression_score. Detector trained on curated historical changes (labels: regression / non-regression).

7) Triage output: for regressions above threshold, bundle top 10 traces (with inputs, outputs, baseline vs current diffs), cause hints (high miss-rate in KV cache, large microbatch amplification), and suggested mitigations (reduce batch timeout, lower microbatch, increase TTL).
8) Post-processing: write results to S3, update dashboard, and emit issue if needed.
comments: 2026-03-05 Marco Reyes: Created ticket — initial spike completed. Ran small 120-point grid locally; saw a cluster of regressions when prefix_cache_ttl_s < 60s combined with microbatch_size >= 8.

2026-03-06 Aisha Patel: POC regression detector (random forest) trained on 180 labeled historical changes. Initial precision 0.77, recall 0.84. Plan to iterate features (add token-level hit-rate deltas).

2026-03-07 Design review (Kriti S): requested example-output diff UI in dashboard and emphasized per-customer segmentation for high-value customers. Adding two new labels to dataset to capture 'enterprise' vs 'standard' traffic.

2026-03-08 Marco Reyes: Prototype CronJob created, PR #811 opened. Benchmarked nightly run on small cluster: 600 points estimated to take ~3.5h on current test cluster — need to optimize by pruning heuristics or move to spot-scaling for night runs.

2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: Updated detector features and retrained; precision bumped to 0.82 on validation. Added additional checks to avoid flagging regressions caused by model rollouts (we filter by model_version in metadata).
2026-03-10 Marco Reyes: Demo to runtime-eng tomorrow. Next actions: finalize pruning heuristic (importance sampling of grid), wire Slack alert + auto-issue creation, and add local triage CLI.
